news.author: CNN
news.article_content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly stepped down last week after a scandal involving extramarital affairs, said Tuesday he would be “honored” to return to the role if the board were to allow it. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.

I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” Huang said in a statement. He stepped down last week from the company he co-founded 33 years ago, ending an extraordinary run at the helm of one of the world’s most valuable companies. The resignation came just four days after the company’s board announced it was investigating him, following reports that he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, who sources have identified as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; as well as reports of another affair with an Nvidia executive.

CNN’s numerous attempts to reach Alice Huang for comment have been unsuccessful. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Jensen Huang said in the statement, noting support he’s received.

CNN has reached out to Nvidia for comment on Huang’s statement. The company’s board of directors, however, is not considering reinstating Huang, a source familiar with the situation told CNN. President Donald Trump, who frequently looked to Huang for guidance on the nation’s AI policies, said Monday he “would not mind” if Huang returned as CEO.

Trump is scheduled to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later in the week. The president said he “may” discuss Nvidia with Xi. Beyond Trump, Huang has seen a strong showing of support in recent days – both from current and former Nvidia employees and across Silicon Valley.

Elon Musk said in a post on X that he would be “honored” to hire Huang. The Tesla and SpaceX CEO also said he would be signing a growing petition for Nvidia’s board to bring back Huang. Big questions loom.

Answers could soon come The US intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between Alice Huang and the Chinese government. Multiple sources have told CNN that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing.

Nvidia is synonymous with the global AI boom, supplying some of the most advanced chips that power AI models for some of the world’s largest technology companies. On Thursday, Nvidia announced its Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as the company’s interim CEO while the board considers internal and external candidates.

Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress in a hearing scheduled for December 1, and Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, will testify the following day. Both will be closed-door hearings with transcribed interviews subsequently released to the public. Huang previously apologized to his family and Nvidia employees in a company message last week, acknowledging that he had been unfaithful to his wife and saying he would cooperate with an independent investigation initiated by the company’s board of directors.

“I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security,” he said last week. Alice Huang is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company and Nvidia customer.

news.article_content_zh:
英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋上周因婚外情丑闻突然辞职，他周二表示，如果董事会允许，他将“很荣幸”重返这一职位。 “我没有达到 NVIDIA 每个人的期望标准，而且我在个人生活中犯了严重错误。

黄在一份声明中表示：“我给董事会带来了问题，对此我深感遗憾。”他上周从这家他 33 年前共同创立的公司辞职，结束了他执掌全球最有价值公司之一的非凡历程。就在四天前，公司董事会宣布对他进行调查。此前有报道称，他与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有多起婚外情，其中包括与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的婚外情，消息人士称她是潜在的中国情报资产；还有报道称，他与英伟达 (Nvidia) 的一名高管发生了另一起婚外情。

美国有线电视新闻网多次尝试联系黄爱丽发表评论，但均未成功。黄仁勋在声明中表示：“如果董事会认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”他指出了他所获得的支持。

美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 已联系英伟达，请其对黄仁勋的声明发表评论。然而，一位知情人士告诉 CNN，该公司董事会并未考虑恢复黄的职位。唐纳德·特朗普总统经常向黄仁勋寻求有关国家人工智能政策的指导，他周一表示，如果黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官，他“不会介意”。

特朗普定于本周晚些时候会见中国领导人习近平。总统表示，他“可能”与习近平讨论英伟达的问题。除了特朗普之外，黄仁勋最近几天还得到了来自英伟达现任和前任员工以及整个硅谷的强烈支持。

埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，他将“很荣幸”雇用黄。这位特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官还表示，他将签署一份越来越多的请愿书，要求英伟达董事会召回黄仁勋。大问题迫在眉睫。

答案很快就会揭晓 美国情报界仍在努力了解黄爱丽与中国政府之间的关系。多个消息来源告诉美国有线电视新闻网，迄今为止收集到的有关她的情报并不能证明她是北京的间谍。

英伟达是全球人工智能热潮的代名词，为一些全球最大的科技公司提供一些最先进的芯片，为人工智能模型提供支持。周四，英伟达宣布首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)将担任公司临时首席执行官，同时董事会考虑内部和外部候选人。

黄仁勋已同意在定于 12 月 1 日举行的国会听证会上作证，英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特 (Tim Teter) 将于第二天作证。这两场听证会都将是闭门听证会，随后将向公众发布采访记录。黄先生上周在公司信息中向家人和英伟达员工道歉，承认自己对妻子不忠，并表示将配合公司董事会发起的独立调查。

“我热爱我们的国家和我们的公司。我致力于保护 NVIDIA 并支持美国的国家安全，”他上周表示。 Alice Huang 是新加坡科技公司 Megaspeed 的前高管，也是 Nvidia 的客户。

一些美国消息人士称，无论她是否被中国情报部门招募，她都会构成反情报风险，因为中国国家安全法要求其公民在接到要求时协助情报收集工作。人们越来越担心 Megaspeed 购买的芯片被转移到中国实体，从而可能绕过美国的出口限制。

Megaspeed否认有任何不当行为，称其是一家“合规且合法的公司”，并将配合美国的调查。英伟达在给 CNN 的一份声明中表示，非法芯片转移的指控“已于去年得到彻底调查并被揭穿”。中国外交部称有关黄爱丽是中国间谍的指控是“毫无根据的猜测，企图抹黑和中伤中国”。英伟达计划于周二晚些时候公布第三季度收益，并随后与分析师举行电话会议，这将是公众第一次有机会直接听取该公司新领导层的讲话。

news.title: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff
news.title_en: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff

inline_images.caption: Evaluation of GPT-6 Astra’s inbox tasks by physicians using maximum reasoning effort. | Image: OpenAI
inline_images.alt: Evaluation of GPT-6 Astra’s inbox tasks by physicians using maximum reasoning effort. | Image: OpenA

news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI wants GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna to click and type their way through clinic software and insurance portals as digital clerks. GPT-6 Luna handles administrative tasks for about 8.5 cents per task, according to the company.

In a recent product announcement, OpenAI targets the lack of APIs in healthcare. The computer-use agents integrated into the Agents API in late September operate existing user interfaces the way a human would. In this case, they transfer data between electronic health records and external web portals.

According to OpenAI, when a patient reports back pain, the agent is meant to search relevant prior findings and draft both an MRI order and a reply to the patient. It should also prepare a prior authorization request on the insurer's portal. Clinicians and the responsible administrative staff review these drafts before they are released. The features are available through the API as well as in ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Clinicians.Ad

In an evaluation described by OpenAI, GPT-6 Astra worked through tasks from electronic health record inboxes, among other things preparing an ibuprofen dosage for a child with a broken arm. Physician reviewers rated 99 percent of the 325 tasks evaluated as clinically safe. In 93 percent of 646 reviews, the reviewers called the prep work very or extremely helpful.

For administrative workflows such as prior authorizations, appeals, or medical equipment orders, OpenAI points to the independent HealthAdminBench benchmark from Stanford University researchers. GPT-6 Astra scored 94.3 percent of possible points. GPT-6 Luna, built for low API pricing, scored 91.8 percent and, according to OpenAI, cost about 8.5 cents per task, 98 percent less than Astra. Both models ran at maximum reasoning effort on the benchmark.Ad

Several partner organizations are helping advance the technology. At CVS Health, the agents already process referrals and specialist consultations across separate systems. According to the announcement, one agent cleared a months-long backlog of outgoing documents in one weekend, while another handles the system steps for tens of thousands of consultations daily. CVS Health published its software architecture as Agent Kit on GitHub.

At insurer Cigna Healthcare, the models merge patient information from more than 10 separate systems. Abridge is developing the agents for planned use in clinical discharge planning. Ambience has demonstrated additional safety mechanisms in which an agent stops when a patient's record is unclear and asks a physician for input. Startups like Assort also use the feature in Codex to complete referrals in practice management software whose APIs don't support that final click.Ad

Because the agents work directly in electronic health records, protecting sensitive health data is a core concern. OpenAI says it does not use organizational data to train its base models. ChatGPT for Healthcare offers role-based access controls and audit logs, according to the company. Organizations can also configure the applications and environments so an agent only accesses the records and actions needed for a given task.Ad

For HIPAA-compliant workflows with protected health information, organizations must sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with OpenAI. They also need to use the covered services and apply the required security and retention settings. news.article_content_zh:
OpenAI 希望 GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6 Luna 作为数字文员通过诊所软件和保险门户进行点击和打字。据该公司称，GPT-6 Luna 处理管理任务的费用约为每项任务 8.5 美分。

在最近的产品公告中，OpenAI 针对医疗保健领域缺乏 API 的问题。九月下旬，计算机使用的代理集成到代理 API 中，以人类的方式操作现有的用户界面。在这种情况下，他们在电子健康记录和外部门户网站之间传输数据。

根据 OpenAI 的说法，当患者报告背痛时，代理将搜索相关的先前发现并起草 MRI 命令和对患者的答复。它还应该在保险公司的门户网站上准备一份事先授权请求。临床医生和负责的行政人员在发布这些草案之前会对其进行审查。这些功能可通过 API 以及 ChatGPT for Healthcare 和 ChatGPT for Clinicians 中使用。

在 OpenAI 描述的一项评估中，GPT-6 Astra 完成了电子健康记录收件箱中的任务，其中包括为手臂骨折的儿童准备布洛芬剂量。医生评审员将 325 项评估任务中的 99% 评为临床安全。在 646 条评论中，93% 的评论者认为准备工作非常或极其有帮助。

对于行政工作流程，如事先授权、上诉或医疗设备订单，OpenAI指向斯坦福大学研究人员的独立HealthAdminBench基准。GPT-6 Astra得分为94.3%。GPT-6 Luna采用低API定价，得分为91.8%，根据OpenAI的数据，每个任务的成本约为8.5美分，比Astra低98%。两个模型在基准测试中都以最大的推理能力运行。广告

一些合作伙伴组织正在帮助推进这项技术。在 CVS Health，代理已经跨不同的系统处理转诊和专家咨询。公告称，一名工作人员在一个周末清理了长达数月积压的外发文件，另一名工作人员每天处理数万次咨询的系统步骤。 CVS Health 在 GitHub 上发布了其软件架构作为 Agent Kit。

在保险公司 Cigna Healthcare，这些模型合并了来自 10 多个独立系统的患者信息。 Abridge 正在开发用于临床出院计划的药物。 Ambience 已经展示了额外的安全机制，当患者的记录不清楚时，代理会停止并询问医生输入信息。像 Assort 这样的初创公司也使用 Codex 中的功能来完成实践管理软件中的推荐，但其 API 不支持最终点击。

由于代理直接在电子健康记录中工作，因此保护敏感的健康数据是一个核心问题。 OpenAI 表示，它不会使用组织数据来训练其基础模型。据该公司称，ChatGPT for Healthcare 提供基于角色的访问控制和审核日志。组织还可以配置应用程序和环境，以便代理仅访问给定任务所需的记录和操作。

对于具有受保护健康信息的符合 HIPAA 的工作流程，组织必须与 OpenAI 签署业务合作协议 (BAA)。他们还需要使用涵盖的服务并应用所需的安全和保留设置。医疗机构本身有责任正确使用，但 OpenAI 作为缔约方，也有 HIPAA 规定的自己的义务。在美国使用 ChatGPT for Clinicians（一项免费的个人计划）的经过验证的医疗专业人员也可以签署 BAA，尽管它仅适用于协议涵盖的功能。

据 OpenAI 称，在 CVS Health 部署中，数据保留在 CVS 控制的基础设施内。 CVS 通过屏幕截图和操作日志来审查代理的工作步骤。该公告没有说明这些屏幕截图的处理位置或存储时间。它也没有涉及欧洲通用数据保护条例（GDPR）。到目前为止，该产品的目标市场是美国市场。

OpenAI 将该技术主要定位为在高度分散的医疗保健系统中应对行政摩擦的工具。是否会被广泛采用并不仅仅取决于该公司公告中引用的准确率和成本。同样具有决定性意义的是代理与现有系统的连接有多可靠，以及人工智能代理在实践中是否可以得到可靠的监控。另一个悬而未决的问题是，是否需要人类决定临床或法律相关的步骤。

news.title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
news.title_en: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Chinese companies have been skirting US export bans by legally renting Nvidia computing power in third countries. After Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, the US is closing that loophole. An investigation also reveals how China has cushioned the years-long chip embargo through an entire industry built around model distillation.

For years, the US has tried to cut China off from importing advanced AI processors through strict export controls. Chinese companies responded by exploiting an entirely legal loophole, renting the computing power they needed through cloud-based remote access from foreign data centers that were allowed to receive US hardware.

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) at the US Commerce Department now wants to shut down that workaround with an interim rule. It aligns remote-access rules with existing physical export bans. Data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil will need a US government license to buy advanced AI chips from US manufacturers like Nvidia, Bloomberg reports. Applications will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

Subsidiaries of US-headquartered companies are exempt from the license requirement, as are shipments to data centers running only commercial recommendation systems for online retailers or social media platforms. The rules take effect once published in the Federal Register. Nvidia's stock fell as much as 2.9 percent after the announcement, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped up to 5.5 percent.

The political trigger, though, was suspected illegal smuggling of physical chips. The new rule comes just days after the abrupt resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who had admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former manager at Singapore-based Megaspeed International. US authorities suspect Alice Huang, who now lives in China, of espionage. They are investigating Megaspeed for possible export-control violations after banned Nvidia chips reportedly turned up in a Chinese data center linked to her. Megaspeed denies any wrongdoing, and President Donald Trump said Monday that Jensen Huang did not compromise national security.

The scandal still set off an open power struggle in Washington over lax enforcement of chip sanctions. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had delayed a Trump-authorized measure against illegal chip diversions, according to Axios, prompting Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to publicly accuse him of inaction. The Commerce Department's announcement now states with unusual bluntness that the draft rule was written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council.

A separate exclusive Reuters investigation shows how Chinese developers cope with the years-long shortage of top-tier domestic hardware. By reviewing more than 300 Chinese papers, patents, job postings, and government documents, Reuters shows for the first time how heavily China relies on model distillation as a stopgap. What started years ago as an academic workaround has grown into an industrial sector with a highly developed division of labor.

The technique does not make powerful chips like Nvidia's unnecessary, but it drastically reduces developers' own compute load because a single expensive query to a US teacher model replaces repeated computation. news.article_content_zh:
中国公司一直在通过在第三国合法租用英伟达计算能力来规避美国的出口禁令。英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职后，美国正在堵住这一漏洞。一项调查还揭示了中国如何通过围绕模型蒸馏建立的整个行业来缓解长达数年的芯片禁运。

多年来，美国一直试图通过严格的出口管制来阻止中国进口先进人工智能处理器。中国公司的回应是利用完全合法的漏洞，通过从被允许接收美国硬件的外国数据中心进行基于云的远程访问来租用他们所需的计算能力。

美国商务部工业与安全局 (BIS) 现在希望通过一项临时规则来终止这一解决办法。它将远程访问规则与现有的物理出口禁令保持一致。据彭博社报道，新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西的数据中心运营商需要获得美国政府许可才能从 Nvidia 等美国制造商购买先进的人工智能芯片。申请将根据具体情况进行审核。

总部位于美国的公司的子公司不受许可证要求的约束，向仅运行在线零售商或社交媒体平台的商业推荐系统的数据中心的货物也不受许可证要求的约束。这些规则一旦在联邦公报上公布即生效。消息公布后，英伟达股价下跌 2.9%，费城半导体指数下跌 5.5%。

不过，政治导火索是涉嫌非法走私物理芯片。这项新规定是在英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋突然辞职几天后出台的，黄仁勋承认与新加坡 Megaspeed International 前经理 Alice Huang 有染。美国当局怀疑现居住在中国的爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 从事间谍活动。据报道，在与 Megaspeed 有关的一个中国数据中心发现了被禁的 Nvidia 芯片后，他们正在调查 Megaspeed 是否可能违反出口管制。 Megaspeed 否认有任何不当行为，唐纳德·特朗普总统周一表示，黄仁勋没有损害国家安全。

该丑闻仍在华盛顿因芯片制裁执行不力而引发公开的权力斗争。据 Axios 称，商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克推迟了特朗普授权的打击非法芯片转移的措施，促使财政部长斯科特·贝森特公开指责他不作为。美国商务部现在的声明异常直白地指出，该规则草案是由财政部和国家安全委员会起草并在其指导下制定的。

路透社的另一项独家调查显示了中国开发商如何应对多年来顶级国产硬件的短缺。通过审查 300 多篇中国论文、专利、招聘信息和政府文件，路透社首次展示了中国对模型蒸馏作为权宜之计的依赖程度。几年前开始的一种学术解决方法已经发展成为一个具有高度发达分工的工业部门。

该技术并不需要像 Nvidia 这样强大的芯片，但它极大地减少了开发人员自己的计算负载，因为对美国教师模型的一次昂贵的查询取代了重复的计算。中国公司现在开发自己的软件，自动从美国领先模型中提取答案、代码和问题解决方案。然后，专业工人处理这些材料来训练更小、更便宜的当地学生模型。

研究论文表明这种做法已经深入人心。早在2024年11月，上海交通大学的研究人员就为阿里巴巴的Qwen2.5-72B创建了10750个训练样本。他们借鉴了 OpenAI o1 的约 5,000 条回复和 GPT-4o mini 的翻译，尽管他们自己当时警告称，对外部创新的依赖迫在眉睫。阿里巴巴于 2025 年 4 月描述了其系统地使用 GPT-4 和 GPT-4o 来进行外语训练数据。2026 年 2 月，交通大学和食品配送公司美团使用 GPT-4o 来训练用于协调编码代理的较小模型。

来自北京的政策指令正在推动这一增长。政府希望在中国制造业部署更小、低成本的人工智能系统。政府官方文件并没有直接指示任何人复制美国模式。尽管如此，八个部委在一月份发布的“人工智能+制造”一揽子计划以及上海和深圳的举措明确推广了蒸馏和其他减少计算需求的技术。在实践中，这种国家驱动的效率推动促使中国开发者大规模利用最强大的美国模型作为数据源。

美国官员早在 7 月就在成都与中国监管机构对峙，因为华盛顿认为大规模蒸馏是中国人工智能快速追赶的主要原因。中国内部人士还指出了他们自己在算法和模型设计方面的进步。财政部长贝森特现在威胁说，如果秘密蒸馏攻击越界成为知识产权盗窃行为，将实施制裁并指定实体名单。中国开发商对这些规则并不确定，最近要求北京工业部提供有关使用外国模式的明确指导方针。

news.title: Sources: Jensen Huang's daughter Madison, a marketing director, helped steer Nvidia's response to Megaspeed scrutiny and temporarily sidelined a top comms exec (Financial Times)
news.title_en: Sources: Jensen Huang's daughter Madison, a marketing director, helped steer Nvidia's response to Megaspeed scrutiny and temporarily sidelined a top comms exec (Financial Times)
news.author: Financial Times
news.article_content:
Madison Huang has emerged as an increasingly powerful figure inside Nvidia, just as the company searches for her father's successor. Huang, daughter of former CEO Jensen Huang, has rapidly risen to the role of senior director of product marketing for physical AI and has accumulated influence far beyond her title, former employees told Business Insider.

After joining the company in 2020, one said they began to see her influence expand in late 2023. "Madison is her father's daughter — she's flinty, she's sharp, she's not a wallflower," another former employee said. "She's out there in front asking questions and changing things." She could assume an even bigger leadership role at Nvidia in the future, two former employees said, but lacks the technical experience to replace her father now that a successor is needed.

Huang's background is predominantly in business and marketing. One said they could have imagined her taking the helm in a decade, but did not have the expertise to guide Nvidia's technology strategy anytime soon. An Nvidia colleague said Huang could strongly hold her own in technical discussions without an engineering background.

They said her role is to help shape how Nvidia brings its technology to market. The scrutiny comes as Jensen Huang exits Nvidia amid revelations of extramarital affairs and a board investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. In addition to choosing a new CEO, Nvidia now faces questions about how to reorganize its leadership.

"We don't know exactly how it's going to be reconfigured, but obviously things will have to change," Huang's colleague added. Huang isn't the only family member at Nvidia. Her brother Spencer Huang works in robotics as a director of product management.

Two former employees described him as having a lower profile than his sister. A classically trained chef, Huang has said she initially planned to study electrical engineering like her parents, but her father encouraged her to pursue something she was "really passionate about." She attended the Culinary Institute of America, worked as a chef and sommelier, and later moved into hospitality marketing at luxury conglomerate LVMH before joining Nvidia as an MBA intern in 2020.

According to Nvidia's annual filing, she took home $1.23 million in compensation this last fiscal year. Huang's husband, Nico Caprez, also works at Nvidia as vice president of global AI infrastructure growth. Huang has become increasingly visible outside the company.

During a trip to South Korea this spring, she met with executives from tech giants such as Samsung and SK Hynix and spoke to students at Seoul National University, where she described leadership as "being in service of others." Huang said working at Nvidia was initially "very intimidating for me because I have no technical background and I'm surrounded by the world's greatest engineers." She kept a running Google Doc of unfamiliar terms and spent hours after work researching them.

news.article_content_en:
Madison Huang has emerged as an increasingly powerful figure inside Nvidia, just as the company searches for her father's successor. Huang, daughter of former CEO Jensen Huang, has rapidly risen to the role of senior director of product marketing for physical AI and has accumulated influence far beyond her title, former employees told Business Insider.

After joining the company in 2020, one said they began to see her influence expand in late 2023. "Madison is her father's daughter — she's flinty, she's sharp, she's not a wallflower," another former employee said. "She's out there in front asking questions and changing things." She could assume an even bigger leadership role at Nvidia in the future, two former employees said, but lacks the technical experience to replace her father now that a successor is needed.

Huang's background is predominantly in business and marketing. One said they could have imagined her taking the helm in a decade, but did not have the expertise to guide Nvidia's technology strategy anytime soon. An Nvidia colleague said Huang could strongly hold her own in technical discussions without an engineering background.

They said her role is to help shape how Nvidia brings its technology to market. The scrutiny comes as Jensen Huang exits Nvidia amid revelations of extramarital affairs and a board investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. In addition to choosing a new CEO, Nvidia now faces questions about how to reorganize its leadership.

"We don't know exactly how it's going to be reconfigured, but obviously things will have to change," Huang's colleague added. Huang isn't the only family member at Nvidia. Her brother Spencer Huang works in robotics as a director of product management.

Two former employees described him as having a lower profile than his sister. A classically trained chef, Huang has said she initially planned to study electrical engineering like her parents, but her father encouraged her to pursue something she was "really passionate about." She attended the Culinary Institute of America, worked as a chef and sommelier, and later moved into hospitality marketing at luxury conglomerate LVMH before joining Nvidia as an MBA intern in 2020.

According to Nvidia's annual filing, she took home $1.23 million in compensation this last fiscal year. Huang's husband, Nico Caprez, also works at Nvidia as vice president of global AI infrastructure growth. Huang has become increasingly visible outside the company.

During a trip to South Korea this spring, she met with executives from tech giants such as Samsung and SK Hynix and spoke to students at Seoul National University, where she described leadership as "being in service of others." Huang said working at Nvidia was initially "very intimidating for me because I have no technical background and I'm surrounded by the world's greatest engineers." She kept a running Google Doc of unfamiliar terms and spent hours after work researching them.

"You have to have some self-resilience and commit yourself to educating yourself on the side," she said at Seoul National University. Her reach extends into Nvidia's startup ecosystem. Genspark cofounder Wen Sang praised her for supporting smaller AI companies and told Business Insider that she introduced his company to Nvidia's chief marketing officer for a product pitch opportunity.

She has taken on a role in major Nvidia partnerships, including collaborations with Foxconn to use AI to design and automate factories and with LG on robotics and data centers. An Nvidia partner who works closely with Huang said she was a "driving force" in establishing a technology standards group called the Alliance for OpenUSD, and helped guide technical discussions among members.

"There is depth, there is breadth, and there is most definitely technical knowledge," they said. Huang's colleague at Nvidia said her responsibilities have become increasingly cross-functional because of her ability to coordinate product launches across engineering, marketing, and other teams.

"She's probably, after Jensen, the hardest-working person I've ever seen in my life," they said. Her close relationship with her father has also given her a unique edge. One former employee cited her ability to anticipate his needs while traveling with him to high-level meetings and appearances, while another said she had become a point of contact for employees seeking access to him.

"She's like a little mini Jensen, his eyes and ears inside the business," a third former employee said. Her growing influence has changed how some teams operate, and she has also clashed with Nvidia veterans and senior executives, three former employees said. Nvidia traditionally empowered a project's designated leader, known as the "pilot in command," to make decisions, one person said.

They added that as Huang gained influence, teams sometimes put off decisions until she joined meetings, even when senior executives or subject-matter experts were present. Huang's colleague at Nvidia said that disagreements are common and employees are encouraged to pursue "intellectual honesty." "She's humble, she's collaborative," the Nvidia partner said, "but most definitely you know things are going to get done."

news.article_content_zh:
就在英伟达寻找她父亲的继任者之际，麦迪逊·黄已成为英伟达内部日益强大的人物。前员工告诉 Business Insider，前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的女儿黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 已迅速晋升为物理人工智能产品营销高级总监，积累的影响力远远超出了她的头衔。

2020 年加入公司后，有人表示，他们在 2023 年底开始看到她的影响力扩大。“麦迪逊是她父亲的女儿——她冷酷、敏锐，不是壁花，”另一位前员工表示。 “她在前面提出问题并改变事情。”两名前员工表示，她未来可能会在英伟达担任更重要的领导角色，但由于需要继任者，她缺乏技术经验来取代她的父亲。

黄的背景主要是商业和营销。一位人士表示，他们本可以想象她在十年内掌舵，但缺乏短期内指导英伟达技术战略的专业知识。一位英伟达同事表示，黄在没有工程背景的情况下也能在技术讨论中保持自己的立场。

他们表示，她的职责是帮助塑造英伟达如何将其技术推向市场。此次审查正值黄仁勋因婚外情被曝光以及董事会调查他是否成为外国情报机构的目标而退出英伟达之际。除了选择新的首席执行官之外，英伟达现在还面临着如何重组领导层的问题。

“我们不知道具体如何重新配置​​，但显然事情必须改变，”黄的同事补充道。黄仁勋并不是英伟达唯一的家族成员。她的兄弟 Spencer Huang 在机器人领域工作，担任产品管理总监。

两名前雇员称他比他姐姐低调。黄是一名受过古典训练的厨师，她说她最初计划像父母一样学习电气工程，但她的父亲鼓励她追求她“真正热衷”的东西。她就读于美国烹饪学院，担任厨师和侍酒师，后来在奢侈品集团 LVMH 从事酒店营销工作，然后于 2020 年作为 MBA 实习生加入 Nvidia。

根据英伟达的年度报告，她在上一财年获得了 123 万美元的薪酬。黄的丈夫 Nico Caprez 也在 Nvidia 担任全球人工智能基础设施发展副总裁。黄在公司外部的知名度越来越高。

今年春天访问韩国期间，她会见了三星和 SK 海力士等科技巨头的高管，并向首尔国立大学的学生发表讲话，她将领导力描述为“为他人服务”。黄仁勋表示，在 Nvidia 工作最初“对我来说非常令人生畏，因为我没有技术背景，而且我周围都是世界上最伟大的工程师”。她保留了一份包含不熟悉术语的运行谷歌文档，并在下班后花几个小时研究它们。

她在首尔国立大学说：“你必须有一定的自我恢复能力，并致力于自我教育。”她的影响力延伸到了英伟达的创业生态系统。 Genspark 联合创始人 Wen Sang 称赞她支持小型人工智能公司，并告诉《商业内幕》，她向 Nvidia 首席营销官介绍了他的公司，以获得产品推介机会。

她在 Nvidia 的主要合作伙伴关系中发挥了重要作用，包括与富士康合作使用人工智能来设计和自动化工厂，以及与 LG 合作开发机器人和数据中心。一位与黄密切合作的英伟达合作伙伴表示，她是建立名为 OpenUSD 联盟的技术标准组织的“推动力”，并帮助指导成员之间的技术讨论。

“有深度，有广度，而且绝对有技术知识，”他们说。黄在英伟达的同事表示，由于她有能力协调工程、营销和其他团队的产品发布，她的职责变得越来越跨职能。

“她可能是继詹森之后我一生中见过的最勤奋的人，”他们说。她与父亲的亲密关系也给了她独特的优势。一名前员工表示，她有能力在与他一起参加高层会议和露面时预测他的需求，而另一名前员工则表示，她已成为寻求与他接触的员工的联系人。

“她就像一个小詹森，他的眼睛和耳朵都在企业内部，”第三位前雇员说。三名前员工表示，她日益增长的影响力改变了一些团队的运作方式，而且她还与英伟达资深人士和高级管理人员发生了冲突。一位人士表示，英伟达传统上会授权项目指定的领导者（即“指挥飞行员”）做出决策。

他们补充说，随着黄的影响力增加，团队有时会推迟决策，直到她参加会议，即使高级管理人员或主题专家在场。黄在英伟达的同事表示，分歧很常见，我们鼓励员工追求“知识上的诚实”。 “她很谦虚，也很善​​于合作，”这位英伟达合作伙伴说道，“但你绝对知道事情一定会完成。”

news.title: Uber and Zipline launch autonomous drone deliveries, starting with Uber Eats customers in Spring, Texas, with plans for 1M deliveries per day by the end of 2029 (Kirsten Korosec/TechCrunch)
news.title_en: Uber and Zipline launch autonomous drone deliveries, starting with Uber Eats customers in Spring, Texas, with plans for 1M deliveries per day by the end of 2029 (Kirsten Korosec/TechCrunch)
news.author: TechCrunch
news.article_content:
Uber Eats customers in a Houston suburb can now have their food delivered by a Zipline drone, the first commercial launch under a partnership announced earlier this year between Uber and the autonomous drone delivery startup.

The commercial partnership kicks off Tuesday in Spring, Texas, before expanding to Dallas. But the companies have far larger ambitions. Uber and Zipline plan to launch drone delivery services in dozens of additional U.S. cities in their collective bid to make one million deliveries per day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

Zipline’s long-range autonomous delivery drones will be used to shuttle food orders weighing up to eight pounds to Uber Eats customers, flying about 300 feet above the ground at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour. Zipline drones don’t land. Instead, the drones lower the orders, which are encased in a small protective pod, to the customer’s location using a tether.

Uber Eats customers in service areas will be able to tap a new “drone” icon on the app’s home page to view all participating restaurants. Uber said that at launch in the Houston area, several nationwide chains, including Jersey Mike’s and Zaxby’s, along with dozens of local restaurants such as Urban Bird and Abu Omar Halal, will offer drone delivery.

“In partnership with Uber Eats we’re going to create a new expectation for delivery in America,” Zipline CEO and co-founder Keller Cliffton said in a statement that underscores those aspirations.

Those nationwide goals mirror the ambitions of other drone delivery companies, including Alphabet-owned Wing and Amazon’s Prime Air service. And those plans have started to collide with concerns from residents in some locations who complain about noise and worry that the drones will disrupt wildlife and pose a risk to safety and privacy.

Companies trying to scale in this nascent industry have argued that delivery via drone is a net benefit for society, citing advantages such as traffic reduction. Customers won’t need to hop in their cars and drive to the store for that forgotten item or takeout order, instead relying on a drone, industry proponents have said.

And while Zipline and other companies have been developing their drones for years, the industry is still in its early days, as is adoption in the communities where services are available.

Zipline, which was founded in 2014, has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software. The California-based company’s initial focus was delivering blood in Rwanda, but it eventually expanded its scope to the United States. Its business in the U.S. scaled quickly after receiving its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration in 2022, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to conduct long-range commercial drone deliveries.

Uber’s partnership extends beyond a commercial relationship with Zipline. The ride-hailing giant also invested in the startup. Neither company has disclosed the investment amount, but Zipline announced last week it had raised $1.5 billion in a round led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, and included backing by Uber, among others.

news.article_content_zh:
休斯敦郊区的 Uber Eats 优食顾客现在可以使用 Zipline 无人机送货，这是 Uber 与自动无人机送货初创公司今年早些时候宣布的合作伙伴关系的首次商业推出。

商业合作关系于周二在德克萨斯州斯普林市启动，然后扩展到达拉斯。但这些公司有着更大的野心。 Uber 和 Zipline 计划在美国另外数十个城市推出无人机送货服务，共同争取到 2029 年底使用这家初创公司的无人机每天完成 100 万次送货。

Zipline 的远程自动送货无人机将用于将重达 8 磅的食品订单运送给 Uber Eats 优食客户，飞行距离地面约 300 英尺，速度高达每小时 70 英里。滑索无人机不会着陆。相反，无人机使用系绳将包裹在一个小型保护吊舱中的订单降低到客户的位置。

服务区域的 Uber Eats 优食顾客将能够点击应用程序主页上的新“无人机”图标来查看所有参与的餐厅。 Uber 表示，在休斯顿地区推出时，包括 Jersey Mike’s 和 Zaxby’s 在内的几家全国连锁店，以及 Urban Bird 和 Abu Omar Halal 等数十家当地餐厅，将提供无人机送货服务。

Zipline 首席执行官兼联合创始人凯勒·克利夫顿 (Keller Cliffton) 在一份强调这些愿望的声明中表示：“通过与 Uber Eats 优食合作，我们将为美国的配送创造新的期望。”

这些全国性目标反映了其他无人机送货公司的雄心，包括 Alphabet 旗下的 Wing 和亚马逊的 Prime Air 服务。这些计划已经开始与一些地方居民的担忧发生冲突，他们抱怨噪音，并担心无人机会扰乱野生动物并对安全和隐私构成风险。

试图在这个新兴行业扩大规模的公司认为，通过无人机送货对社会来说是一项净效益，并列举了减少交通量等优势。行业支持者表示，顾客不再需要开车去商店购买遗忘的商品或外卖订单，而是依靠无人机。

尽管 Zipline 和其他公司多年来一直在开发无人机，但该行业仍处于早期阶段，在提供服务的社区中的采用也是如此。

Zipline 成立于 2014 年，开发了一个无人机送货生态系统，其中包括飞机、发射和着陆系统以及物流软件。这家总部位于加州的公司最初的重点是在卢旺达提供血液，但最终将业务范围扩大到美国。 2022 年获得美国联邦航空管理局第 135 部分航空承运人认证后，该公司在美国的业务迅速扩大，这是授权该公司进行远程商用无人机交付的一个关键监管障碍。

Uber 的合作伙伴关系超出了与 Zipline 的商业关系。这家叫车巨头也投资了这家初创公司。两家公司均未披露投资金额，但 Zipline 上周宣布，已在 Paradigm、WCM Investment Management 和 Layer Global 领投的一轮融资中筹集了 15 亿美元，并得到了 Uber 等公司的支持。

news.title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
news.title_en: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed

inline_images.caption: The gavel in front of the DOJ seal.
inline_images.alt: The gavel in front of the DOJ seal.

news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.

“While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting,” the departments said in a statement issued Monday evening. The departments acknowledged there’s been “significant public attention” on Megaspeed.

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week after reports he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, who Megaspeed says left the company in August 2025. The scandal has raised questions about national security, and sparked scrutiny of Nvidia’s handling of exports of its chips to China and Megaspeed’s possible role in moving along Nvidia’s chips.

Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed “came to a sudden halt” late last year after its investigators received an email from Nvidia’s general counsel, claiming Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler gave Nvidia permission to reach out. The case was then “quickly” handed over to the DOJ, according to the Times.

> After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations. In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list. Based on the Department of Commerce’s investigation, agents from the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang. Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.

The statement doesn’t go into detail about the current status of the case, but it says the DOJ and Commerce Department “will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.”

美国司法部和商务部表示，他们正在调查总部位于新加坡的数据中心公司 Megaspeed，该公司与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的辞职有关，此前有报道称调查已于去年停止。

这些部门在周一晚间发布的一份声明中表示：“虽然我们通常不会对正在进行的调查发表评论，但提供事实并解决公开报告中流传的不准确信息符合公共利益。”这些部门承认 Megaspeed 受到了“公众的高度关注”。

黄上周辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，此前有报道称，他与 Megaspeed 前高管、被指控为中国间谍的黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 有染，Megaspeed 称黄爱丽于 2025 年 8 月离开了公司。这一丑闻引发了有关国家安全的质疑，并引发了对英伟达处理其向中国芯片出口以及 Megaspeed 在运送 Nvidia 芯片方面可能发挥的作用的审查。

本月早些时候，《纽约时报》报道称，去年年底，商务部对 Megaspeed 的调查“突然停止”，原因是调查人员收到了英伟达总法律顾问的一封电子邮件，声称商务部官员杰弗里·凯斯勒允许英伟达进行接触。据《泰晤士报》报道，此案随后“迅速”移交给司法部。

> 在通过主动监控潜在的敏感半导体转移来识别可疑活动后，美国商务部于 2024 年启动了对 Megaspeed 潜在违反出口管制行为的调查。 2025 年 5 月，美国商务部调查人员要求 Nvidia 提供有关直接或间接向 Megaspeed 销售的记录。 2025 年 6 月，Nvidia 将 Megaspeed 列入“禁止出售”名单。根据商务部的调查，商务部工业和安全局的特工与新加坡执法官员一起，于 2025 年 6 月对 Megaspeed 进行了现场、亲自的最终用途检查，并采访了首席执行官 Alice Huang。此次执法行动之后，司法部牵头对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查。

声明没有详细说明案件目前的进展情况，但表示司法部和商务部“将对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。

news.title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
news.title_en: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company’s board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement published by The Wall Street Journal.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, according to the statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

news.title: Sources: NSA Net, the highly classified network that the NSA uses for its internal communications, is down; there is no evidence of a cyberattack (CNN)
news.title_en: Sources: NSA Net, the highly classified network that the NSA uses for its internal communications, is down; there is no evidence of a cyberattack (CNN)
news.author: CNN
news.article_content:
The highly classified network that the National Security Agency uses for its internal communications is down, according to six people familiar with the matter. The network, called NSA Net, allows employees to communicate classified information internally. At this point there is no evidence of a cyberattack, sources said.

As the agency works to understand the scope of the problem, it has enacted staggered arrivals for personnel, the sources said. CNN has asked the National Security Agency for comment. A current and a former US official said an outage at NSA Net would not impact the agency’s ability to communicate urgent intelligence to President Donald Trump while he is traveling in Asia on Air Force One.

Both sources described multiple redundancies and backup networks that the government could use to communicate securely with the president who is currently in the Philippines before heading to China tomorrow for talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The outage at America’s most powerful intelligence agency comes on the heels of multiple major tech glitches affecting airlines and other corporations around the country. All flights nationwide were grounded for hours on Friday after a massive systems failure, leading to thousands of flights being delayed or canceled.

The Federal Aviation Administration traced the problem to a single router in Arkansas. Meanwhile, a massive outage last week affecting Microsoft products left people around the world unable to access Outlook email and Team meetings. There is no indication that the NSA, FAA or Microsoft outages were caused by a cyberattack.

But they are stark examples of how tech failures can roil markets and potentially threaten national security. This story is breaking and will be updated.

news.author: Reuters
news.article_content:
FILE PHOTO: US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speaks to reporters outside the White House after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued a national ground stop "due to extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety" following the agency's earlier report of serious air traffic control communications issues, in Washington, DC, US, November 13, 2026. REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz/File Photo

Nov 17 (Reuters) - The top US homeland security official said Tuesday a series of technology outages are not tied to cyberattacks but rather aging systems that are in need of upgrades.

Disruptions at United Airlines, the Federal Aviation Administration, Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase have raised alarm.

"Some of the technology that they're pushing out there, they're pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system," Markwayne Mullin told CNBC. "But it has nothing to do with cyber attacks, and I believe we're going to see more of this as new technology rolls out."

news.title: Codex, which lets businesses use stablecoins for cross-border payments across Asia, Latin America, and sub-Saharan Africa, raised a $30M Series A led by Pantera (Camila Grigera Naón/Fortune)
news.title_en: Codex, which lets businesses use stablecoins for cross-border payments across Asia, Latin America, and sub-Saharan Africa, raised a $30M Series A led by Pantera (Camila Grigera Naón/Fortune)
news.author: Fortune
news.article_content:
Money might make the world go round—but that doesn’t mean getting it around the world is easy. And while stablecoins, or cryptocurrencies pegged to fiat money, can simplify the process considerably, many businesses still lack the infrastructure to use them for cross-border payments. That’s where Codex sees an opportunity.

The Delaware-based startup announced Tuesday it raised $30 million in a Series A round to help businesses send money across borders and exchange currencies, without the need to deposit money in advance to use the service. Codex aims to carve out a niche in Asia and connect the region to markets in Latin America and sub-Saharan Africa.

“We help people convert money into whatever form they want and give it to whoever they want, wherever they want,” Haonan Li, cofounder and CEO of Codex, told Fortune. “Turns out, in lots of parts of the world, this is actually super hard to do.”

The 35-person company plans to use part of the capital to further automate its foreign-exchange platform, with AI agents central to its vision for how the business will operate, and keep costs down as transaction volumes grow.

Pantera Capital led the round, with participation from Dragonfly and Coinbase Ventures, at a $130 million post-money valuation. Both participated in Codex’s earlier seed round, which Dragonfly led alongside backers Circle Ventures, Cumberland, and Wintermute.

Stablecoins have been one of cryptocurrency’s longest-lasting trends, gaining traction as a lifeline in countries with high inflation or capital controls, and as a low-cost payment tool for businesses. Payments made with stablecoins reached at least $401 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 42% year over year, with businesses on the receiving end of an estimated 58% to 64% of that volume, according to a September report by global consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal.

“[The team] is building Codex to meet the challenge of what happens after this massive explosion of stablecoin issuance, which is… a really fragmented system,” Franklin Bi general partner at Pantera Capital, said.

An economist by training, Li began his career in geopolitical forecasting research for political psychologist and writer Philip Tetlock, followed by a stint in quantitative finance. He later caught the “crypto bug” and became an early employee at Optimism, where he worked on Ethereum scaling and protocol economics.

There, he began to explore crypto’s most practical applications and landed on stablecoins, which some in Ethereum circles dismissed as boring. Li saw a way to help people excluded from traditional financial networks save, transfer, and exchange money.

To build that business, he teamed up with an old friend from his military days. Li had met Victor Yaw, now a Codex cofounder, about a decade earlier in infantry officer candidate school in Singapore’s military. Fellow cofounder Momo Ong, whom Li met through San Francisco’s founder community, initially advised the team before he joined full time. Together, they founded Codex in 2024.

After a few iterations, the company settled on its current product about a year ago. It now has offices in Singapore, Hong Kong and London, as well as New York and San Francisco. As Li put it: “the journey stretched from the jungles of Brunei to the skyscrapers of New York.”

news.article_content_zh:
金钱或许可以让世界运转起来，但这并不意味着让金钱运转起来很容易。尽管稳定币或与法定货币挂钩的加密货币可以大大简化流程，但许多企业仍然缺乏使用它们进行跨境支付的基础设施。这就是 Codex 看到的机会。

这家总部位于特拉华州的初创公司周二宣布，在 A 轮融资中筹集了 3000 万美元，帮助企业跨境汇款和兑换货币，而无需提前存钱即可使用该服务。 Codex 旨在在亚洲开拓市场，并将该地区与拉丁美洲和撒哈拉以南非洲市场连接起来。

Codex 联合创始人兼首席执行官李浩南向《财富》杂志表示：“我们帮助人们将金钱转换成他们想要的任何形式，并随时随地将其送给任何他们想要的人。” “事实证明，在世界许多地方，这实际上是非常难做到的。”

这家拥有 35 名员工的公司计划利用部分资金进一步自动化其外汇平台，人工智能代理将成为其业务运营愿景的核心，并随着交易量的增长降低成本。

Pantera Capital 领投，Dragonfly 和 Coinbase Ventures 跟投，投后估值为 1.3 亿美元。两人都参与了 Codex 的早期种子轮融资，由 Dragonfly 与支持者 Circle Ventures、Cumberland 和 Wintermute 共同领投。

稳定币一直是加密货币最持久的趋势之一，作为高通胀或资本管制国家的生命线以及企业的低成本支付工具而受到关注。根据全球咨询公司 Alvarez & Marsal 9 月份的一份报告，2026 年前 8 个月，使用稳定币支付的金额至少达到 4010 亿美元，同比增长 42%，其中企业接收的金额预计占 58% 至 64%。

Pantera Capital 普通合伙人 Franklin Bi 表示：“[团队]正在构建 Codex，以应对稳定币发行大规模爆炸后所发生的挑战，这是一个非常分散的系统。”

作为一名训练有素的经济学家，李开始了他的职业生涯，为政治心理学家和作家菲利普·泰洛克进行地缘政治预测研究，随后在量化金融领域工作了一段时间。后来他发现了“加密货币错误”，并成为 Optimism 的早期员工，在那里他从事以太坊扩展和协议经济学工作。

在那里，他开始探索加密货币最实际的应用，并最终选择了稳定币，但以太坊圈子里的一些人认为稳定币很无聊。李找到了一种方法来帮助那些被排除在传统金融网络之外的人们储蓄、转移和兑换货币。

为了开展这项业务，他与一位军旅时期的老朋友合作。大约十年前，李在新加坡军队的步兵军官候补学校认识了 Victor Yaw，他现在是 Codex 的联合创始人。李通过旧金山的创始人社区结识了联合创始人之一的 Momo Ong，他在全职加入之前最初为团队提供了建议。他们于 2024 年共同创立了 Codex。

经过几次迭代后，该公司大约一年前确定了当前的产品。目前，该公司在新加坡、香港、伦敦以及纽约和旧金山设有办事处。正如李所说：“旅程从文莱的丛林延伸到纽约的摩天大楼。”

news.title: Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees on December 1, per the leaders of the panels (Garrett Downs/CNBC)
news.title_en: Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees on December 1, per the leaders of the panels (Garrett Downs/CNBC)
news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on Dec. 1, the leaders of those congressional panels said on Tuesday.

Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will also appear before the committees on Dec. 2, a statement from the lawmakers said.

"We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security," said Reps. Brian Mast, R-Fla., John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Rick Crawford, R-Ark., the chairs of the Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence Committees.

"The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia's role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal," they said.

news.title: Mexico Risks Missing Out on AI Data Center Boom as Energy Crunch Bites
news.title_en: Mexico Risks Missing Out on AI Data Center Boom as Energy Crunch Bites
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
The reporting was supported by a grant from the Pulitzer Center.

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — More than three decades after serving in Operation Desert Storm, Loretta Young Thornton never expected the sounds of war to follow her home.

Thornton, 66, spent nearly 25 years in the Tennessee Army National Guard, serving as a military police officer before retiring as a decorated sergeant in 2004. She also built a career with the U.S. Postal Service.

After a lifetime of work, she poured her savings into a modest, four-bedroom home built in the 1920s on a secluded two-acre lot in Memphis, near the Mississippi state line.

When Thornton bought the house in 2014, the surrounding woods were home to deer, squirrels, hawks and wild turkeys. At night, she listened to the calls of owls, including one she affectionately called her boyfriend.

Then the trees came down, sending clouds of dust swirling toward Thornton's home.

In their place rose Colossus 2, a massive data center built for billionaire Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, xAI. The sprawling complex, designed to house thousands of powerful computer chips to train the next generation of AI models, sits just across the railroad tracks from Thornton's property.

Now, the sounds of nature have been replaced by the drone of industrial machinery, a mechanical roar resembling a jet engine that Thornton said runs day and night.

The squirrels have disappeared. The owls have largely fallen silent.

The relentless noise sometimes triggers troubling memories of her military service, forcing Thornton to remind herself that she's no longer in a war zone.

“When I come out here, or when I go to bed at night, I train my thoughts,” she said. “You OK? You at home? Ain't no bomb gonna drop on you. You know you ain't in the desert no more.”

She tries to tune out the noise by working in her yard and renovating her back deck. Humor helps, too.

“I just say that's my noisy neighbor, Elon Musk,” she said.

Thornton is living on the front lines of a data center boom sweeping Tennessee and the nation, as technology companies race to build the infrastructure powering artificial intelligence.

news.summary_en: An electricity grid in need of upgrades and permitting delays have made it harder for Mexico to attract data center investment despite its apparent advantages.
news.article_content_en:
The reporting was supported by a grant from the Pulitzer Center.

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — More than three decades after serving in Operation Desert Storm, Loretta Young Thornton never expected the sounds of war to follow her home.

Thornton, 66, spent nearly 25 years in the Tennessee Army National Guard, serving as a military police officer before retiring as a decorated sergeant in 2004. She also built a career with the U.S. Postal Service.

After a lifetime of work, she poured her savings into a modest, four-bedroom home built in the 1920s on a secluded two-acre lot in Memphis, near the Mississippi state line.

When Thornton bought the house in 2014, the surrounding woods were home to deer, squirrels, hawks and wild turkeys. At night, she listened to the calls of owls, including one she affectionately called her boyfriend.

Then the trees came down, sending clouds of dust swirling toward Thornton's home.

In their place rose Colossus 2, a massive data center built for billionaire Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, xAI. The sprawling complex, designed to house thousands of powerful computer chips to train the next generation of AI models, sits just across the railroad tracks from Thornton's property.

Now, the sounds of nature have been replaced by the drone of industrial machinery, a mechanical roar resembling a jet engine that Thornton said runs day and night.

The squirrels have disappeared. The owls have largely fallen silent.

The relentless noise sometimes triggers troubling memories of her military service, forcing Thornton to remind herself that she's no longer in a war zone.

“When I come out here, or when I go to bed at night, I train my thoughts,” she said. “You OK? You at home? Ain't no bomb gonna drop on you. You know you ain't in the desert no more.”

She tries to tune out the noise by working in her yard and renovating her back deck. Humor helps, too.

“I just say that's my noisy neighbor, Elon Musk,” she said.

Thornton is living on the front lines of a data center boom sweeping Tennessee and the nation, as technology companies race to build the infrastructure powering artificial intelligence.

The Tennessee Valley Authority is planning more than $13 billion in power system investments through 2029. Its long-range forecasts project a need for 11,000 to 32,000 megawatts of additional generating capacity by 2040. Even at the low end, that would expand TVA’s existing power system by roughly one-third. At the high end, it would nearly double its size.

Much of the pressure is coming from electricity-hungry industries like data centers. They already account for 18% of TVA's industrial electricity demand, a share expected to double by 2030, according to the utility's estimates. Industrial customers account for about 60% of the utility's total electricity demand.

But as TVA prepares for one of the largest power expansions in its history, the public doesn't know how much of that projected growth is tied to data centers.

Last year, TVA reported roughly 11,000 megawatts of electricity requests from data centers and technology companies alone, nearly a third of its existing generating capacity. That's enough power to supply roughly 6.4 million average homes, according to TVA's estimates. It's just over double the total number of households in Tennessee.

TVA now calls that figure outdated and has declined to provide an updated estimate or disclose how much data center demand is included in its power forecasts.

Spokesman Scott Brooks described the earlier figure as a "moment in time" that was "likely outdated as soon as it was shared."

Meanwhile, economists warn of a possible AI investment bubble. If the boom goes bust, who pays for billions in power infrastructure built to serve demand that never materializes?

TVA says new charges on data centers will help protect customers. But environmental advocates question whether those safeguards go far enough.

“If they are not getting revenues to cover these costs from the data centers, they will get them from the rest of us,” said Maggie Shober, research director of the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy.

From Nashville to Memphis, communities across Tennessee are fighting back against the data center boom.

Hundreds protested a proposed facility near the Nashville Zoo this year, while in rural Lawrenceburg, residents packed a planning commission meeting to oppose another project. In Memphis, a debate over a proposed moratorium erupted into chaotic protests that shut down a city council meeting.

The battles are unfolding amid a nationwide building frenzy. The United States already has more than 4,000 data centers, according to industry database Data Center Map. Those facilities consumed more than 4% of the nation's electricity in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency, which projects demand will more than double by 2030. A Pew Research Center analysis found that much of the planned construction is headed to rural America.

These facilities are essentially giant warehouses packed with computer servers. The largest operate thousands of powerful chips around the clock, requiring enormous amounts of electricity and cooling.

Data centers have been around for decades, but the artificial intelligence boom is ushering in a new generation of sprawling, power-hungry campuses that dwarf many of their predecessors.

Tennessee has about 65 data centers of varying sizes, including major campuses operated by xAI in Memphis, Meta in Gallatin and Google in Clarksville, according to Data Center Map.

More massive projects are being proposed. They include a $659 million expansion of xAI's Colossus 2 campus in Memphis and an $11.3 billion, 850-acre development in Bradley County outside Chattanooga known as Project River, which proposes generating up to 1,500 megawatts of its own electricity to power a hyperscale data center.

As TVA moves ahead with new power generation, its board gathered in Memphis in August to approve protections intended to keep data center costs from falling on ordinary customers.

Meeting at the Halloran Centre on Aug. 20, board members unanimously approved with no discussion or debate a new electricity rate charging data centers about 10% more than TVA's manufacturing rate.

Officials said the utility has 4,120 megawatts of new generating capacity under construction and another 3,000 megawatts under evaluation. But TVA says it is not building specifically for data centers.

"TVA is not focused on building to meet data center growth," Brooks told The Tennessean. "We are focused on building new generation to support growth in business and industry and to preserve delivery of reliable, affordable electricity to 10 million people we serve."

Under the new rate, which took effect Oct. 1, new and expanding data centers subject to the charge face a nonrefundable capacity commitment fee of approximately $1.5 million per megawatt, payable over three to five years. The charge is intended to recover costs associated with additional power generation needed to serve their demand. TVA can also require data centers to temporarily reduce or interrupt their electricity use.

TVA says the measures protect households and other businesses from subsidizing data center growth.

But environmental advocates say TVA has not provided enough information to determine whether those protections would cover its long-term investments if data centers close early or use less electricity than expected.

Shober with the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy said other major utilities, including Duke Energy and Georgia Power, have disclosed more information about their efforts to protect customers. Those measures include minimum electricity payments and penalties if data centers terminate their contracts early, though Shober said the protections have not always been sufficient.

Shober said TVA's capacity commitment fee could offer stronger safeguards.

"For TVA, this capacity commitment charge in particular indicates it could protect customers," Shober said. "We just don't have enough information to say that with any certainty."

TVA says it based its new data center rates on annual cost-of-service studies, but has not released the calculations showing how it arrived at the roughly 10% rate increase or the $1.5 million-per-megawatt capacity fee. Portions of the rate schedule have surfaced in a federal securities filing, but TVA has not yet fulfilled The Tennessean's request for the full schedule or provided the underlying studies Shober says are needed to evaluate its protections.

Power plants and transmission lines can operate for decades, potentially outlasting the data centers they were built to serve.

A 2025 report commissioned by the Southern Environmental Law Center warned that electricity forecasts may be inflated because developers request power at multiple locations and there may not be enough advanced computer chips to equip all the proposed facilities.

The report, prepared by London Economics International, estimated that planned data centers across much of the United States alone would require 90% of the world's projected increase in AI chip production through 2030, even assuming rapid manufacturing growth.

Amanda Garcia, a senior attorney with the law center, said the findings raise questions about whether utilities are building power infrastructure for demand that may never materialize.

"If the data center demand doesn't materialize because there's a bubble, then ratepayers are going to be on the hook for paying all those costs over the longer term," she said.

Power plants, transmission lines and substations can cost billions to build, with expenses recovered through electricity rates over decades. If data centers close or fail to use as much power as expected, other customers could be left paying for infrastructure built to serve them.

Garcia pointed to TVA's own history as a warning.

In the 1970s, the utility embarked on an ambitious nuclear expansion, planning 17 reactors to meet anticipated growth. But demand fell short of projections as construction costs soared. By 1984, TVA had canceled eight planned reactors, abandoning billions of dollars in investments.

TVA says its long-range planning accounts for uncertainty, including scenarios in which electricity demand grows more slowly than expected. The utility says that it does not assume every proposed data center will be built.

The uncertainty extends far beyond TVA. Economists say America's AI boom could rival the largest infrastructure expansions in the nation's history.

Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, an economist at Columbia Business School, estimates the nation could spend $10 trillion on data centers and related infrastructure by 2032, a greater share of economic output than railroad construction consumed at its peak in the late 1800s.

His research identified 509 gigawatts of proposed data center capacity nationwide, nearly 10 times what's operating today. He estimates a more realistic total of roughly 180 gigawatts by 2032, suggesting most announced projects will never be built.

For now, he said, demand is outpacing supply. The question is when that might change.

"At which point are we beginning to overbuild it?" he asked.

Asad Ramzanali, a researcher with Vanderbilt University's Policy Accelerator, sees another risk: Technology companies are investing hundreds of billions in AI infrastructure without yet generating enough revenue to justify the spending.

"At the core of the AI economy is a basic math problem," he said.

The risks could extend far beyond Silicon Valley, Ramzanali said. While early AI investments were largely funded by technology giants' profits, the expansion increasingly relies on borrowing and outside investors, potentially exposing retirement savings and the broader economy to a downturn.

In a worst-case scenario, he said, losses could spread through financial markets, triggering a crisis reminiscent of the 2008 economic crash.

But the data center industry says demand is strong.

"It's not the dot com boom, because this is steel in the ground," said Christy Tarallo of the Data Center Coalition, pointing to strong demand and low vacancy rates as evidence the boom is sustainable.

Still, she urged communities to scrutinize developers proposing facilities they intend to lease to other companies. Without a committed tenant, she said, local officials have less assurance that a project is financially viable.

A developer unable to answer that question is a "red flag," Tarallo said, adding that responsible operators should be transparent about who will occupy their facilities.

The industry promises communities new investment, tax revenue and jobs. But across the railroad tracks from Musk's xAI facility in Memphis, Loretta Thornton said she has seen little of that prosperity.

On a sweltering afternoon in Memphis, Thornton sat on her front porch as the steady hum of machinery drifted across the railroad tracks.

Her grandchildren can no longer comfortably visit because of the noise, she said.

Thornton has contacted attorneys and community organizations seeking help, without success. She's heard the noise could diminish by 2027, but remains skeptical.

She's giving it another 18 months. If conditions don't improve, she may have to leave the home where she planned to spend the rest of her life. But she wonders who would buy a house next to one of the country's largest data centers.

For now, she has little choice but to live with the noise.

"You have to endure it," she said. "You got to figure out a way to endure it."

This is the first in a three-part investigative series examining how the data center boom is reshaping Tennessee.

They already account for 18% of TVA's industrial electricity demand, a share expected to double by 2030, according to the utility's estimates. Industrial customers account for about 60% of the utility's total electricity demand.
But as TVA prepares for one of the largest power expansions in its history, the public doesn't know how much of that projected growth is tied to data centers.

Last year, TVA reported roughly 11,000 megawatts of electricity requests from data centers and technology companies alone, nearly a third of its existing generating capacity. That's enough power to supply roughly 6.4 million average homes, according to TVA's estimates. It's just over double the total number of households in Tennessee.
TVA now calls that figure outdated and has declined to provide an updated estimate or disclose how much data center demand is included in its power forecasts.
Spokesman Scott Brooks described the earlier figure as a "moment in time" that was "likely outdated as soon as it was shared."
Meanwhile, economists warn of a possible AI investment bubble. If the boom goes bust, who pays for billions in power infrastructure built to serve demand that never materializes?
TVA says new charges on data centers will help protect customers. But environmental advocates question whether those safeguards go far enough.
“If they are not getting revenues to cover these costs from the data centers, they will get them from the rest of us,” said Maggie Shober, research director of the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy.
From Nashville to Memphis, communities across Tennessee are fighting back against the data center boom.

Hundreds protested a proposed facility near the Nashville Zoo this year, while in rural Lawrenceburg, residents packed a planning commission meeting to oppose another project. In Memphis, a debate over a proposed moratorium erupted into chaotic protests that shut down a city council meeting.

The battles are unfolding amid a nationwide building frenzy. The United States already has more than 4,000 data centers, according to industry database Data Center Map. Those facilities consumed more than 4% of the nation's electricity in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency, which projects demand will more than double by 2030. A Pew Research Center analysis found that much of the planned construction is headed to rural America.

These facilities are essentially giant warehouses packed with computer servers. The largest operate thousands of powerful chips around the clock, requiring enormous amounts of electricity and cooling.
Data centers have been around for decades, but the artificial intelligence boom is ushering in a new generation of sprawling, power-hungry campuses that dwarf many of their predecessors.
Tennessee has about 65 data centers of varying sizes, including major campuses operated by xAI in Memphis, Meta in Gallatin and Google in Clarksville, according to Data Center Map.

More massive projects are being proposed. They include a $659 million expansion of xAI's Colossus 2 campus in Memphis and an $11.3 billion, 850-acre development in Bradley County outside Chattanooga known as Project River, which proposes generating up to 1,500 megawatts of its own electricity to power a hyperscale data center.
As TVA moves ahead with new power generation, its board gathered in Memphis in August to approve protections intended to keep data center costs from falling on ordinary customers.
Meeting at the Halloran Centre on Aug. 20, board members unanimously approved with no discussion or debate a new electricity rate charging data centers about 10% more than TVA's manufacturing rate.

Officials said the utility has 4,120 megawatts of new generating capacity under construction and another 3,000 megawatts under evaluation. But TVA says it is not building specifically for data centers.

"TVA is not focused on building to meet data center growth," Brooks told The Tennessean. "We are focused on building new generation to support growth in business and industry and to preserve delivery of reliable, affordable electricity to 10 million people we serve."

Under the new rate, which took effect Oct. 1, new and expanding data centers subject to the charge face a nonrefundable capacity commitment fee of approximately $1.5 million per megawatt, payable over three to five years. The charge is intended to recover costs associated with additional power generation needed to serve their demand. TVA can also require data centers to temporarily reduce or interrupt their electricity use.
TVA says the measures protect households and other businesses from subsidizing data center growth.

But environmental advocates say TVA has not provided enough information to determine whether those protections would cover its long-term investments if data centers close early or use less electricity than expected.

Shober with the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy said other major utilities, including Duke Energy and Georgia Power, have disclosed more information about their efforts to protect customers. Those measures include minimum electricity payments and penalties if data centers terminate their contracts early, though Shober said the protections have not always been sufficient.
Shober said TVA's capacity commitment fee could offer stronger safeguards.
"For TVA, this capacity commitment charge in particular indicates it could protect customers," Shober said. "We just don't have enough information to say that with any certainty."

TVA says it based its new data center rates on annual cost-of-service studies, but has not released the calculations showing how it arrived at the roughly 10% rate increase or the $1.5 million-per-megawatt capacity fee. Portions of the rate schedule have surfaced in a federal securities filing, but TVA has not yet fulfilled The Tennessean's request for the full schedule or provided the underlying studies Shober says are needed to evaluate its protections.
Power plants and transmission lines can operate for decades, potentially outlasting the data centers they were built to serve.

A 2025 report commissioned by the Southern Environmental Law Center warned that electricity forecasts may be inflated because developers request power at multiple locations and there may not be enough advanced computer chips to equip all the proposed facilities.

The report, prepared by London Economics International, estimated that planned data centers across much of the United States alone would require 90% of the world's projected increase in AI chip production through 2030, even assuming rapid manufacturing growth.
Amanda Garcia, a senior attorney with the law center, said the findings raise questions about whether utilities are building power infrastructure for demand that may never materialize.
"If the data center demand doesn't materialize because there's a bubble, then ratepayers are going to be on the hook for paying all those costs over the longer term," she said.

Power plants, transmission lines and substations can cost billions to build, with expenses recovered through electricity rates over decades. If data centers close or fail to use as much power as expected, other customers could be left paying for infrastructure built to serve them.
Garcia pointed to TVA's own history as a warning.

In the 1970s, the utility embarked on an ambitious nuclear expansion, planning 17 reactors to meet anticipated growth. But demand fell short of projections as construction costs soared. By 1984, TVA had canceled eight planned reactors, abandoning billions of dollars in investments.

TVA says its long-range planning accounts for uncertainty, including scenarios in which electricity demand grows more slowly than expected. The utility says that it does not assume every proposed data center will be built.
The uncertainty extends far beyond TVA. Economists say America's AI boom could rival the largest infrastructure expansions in the nation's history.

Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, an economist at Columbia Business School, estimates the nation could spend $10 trillion on data centers and related infrastructure by 2032, a greater share of economic output than railroad construction consumed at its peak in the late 1800s.

His research identified 509 gigawatts of proposed data center capacity nationwide, nearly 10 times what's operating today. He estimates a more realistic total of roughly 180 gigawatts by 2032, suggesting most announced projects will never be built.
For now, he said, demand is outpacing supply. The question is when that might change.
"At which point are we beginning to overbuild it?" he asked.

Asad Ramzanali, a researcher with Vanderbilt University's Policy Accelerator, sees another risk: Technology companies are investing hundreds of billions in AI infrastructure without yet generating enough revenue to justify the spending.
"At the core of the AI economy is a basic math problem," he said.

The risks could extend far beyond Silicon Valley, Ramzanali said. While early AI investments were largely funded by technology giants' profits, the expansion increasingly relies on borrowing and outside investors, potentially exposing retirement savings and the broader economy to a downturn.
In a worst-case scenario, he said, losses could spread through financial markets, triggering a crisis reminiscent of the 2008 economic crash.
But the data center industry says demand is strong.

"It's not the dot com boom, because this is steel in the ground," said Christy Tarallo of the Data Center Coalition, pointing to strong demand and low vacancy rates as evidence the boom is sustainable.

Still, she urged communities to scrutinize developers proposing facilities they intend to lease to other companies. Without a committed tenant, she said, local officials have less assurance that a project is financially viable.
A developer unable to answer that question is a "red flag," Tarallo said, adding that responsible operators should be transparent about who will occupy their facilities.

The industry promises communities new investment, tax revenue and jobs. But across the railroad tracks from Musk's xAI facility in Memphis, Loretta Thornton said she has seen little of that prosperity.
On a sweltering afternoon in Memphis, Thornton sat on her front porch as the steady hum of machinery drifted across the railroad tracks.
Her grandchildren can no longer comfortably visit because of the noise, she said.
Thornton has contacted attorneys and community organizations seeking help, without success. She's heard the noise could diminish by 2027, but remains skeptical.

She's giving it another 18 months. If conditions don't improve, she may have to leave the home where she planned to spend the rest of her life. But she wonders who would buy a house next to one of the country's largest data centers.
For now, she has little choice but to live with the noise.
"You have to endure it," she said. "You got to figure out a way to endure it."
This is the first in a three-part investigative series examining how the data center boom is reshaping Tennessee.

news.title: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments
news.title_en: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI is giving NATO and several European governments access to its cybersecurity tool Daybreak. Through Daybreak, cyber defense teams can use OpenAI's models to audit software, find vulnerabilities, and patch security gaps. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) says it's already using the underlying models heavily. NCIA chief Dylan Browne called it a generational leap in cyber defense. During the NATO exercise Crossed Swords 2026, participants deployed AI agents for cyber operations under human oversight for the first time.

The models have already delivered results elsewhere. The EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA used them to find four vulnerabilities in software used by EU institutions. A joint report with CERT-EU examined 27 software projects, and 95 percent of the 88 reported issues turned out to be real bugs. Poland's CERT Polska found six vulnerabilities in MikroTik routers that were being actively exploited. Ukraine is using Daybreak to protect civilian infrastructure. France, Germany, and Poland have also been granted access.

news.title: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material have surged more than 8,400 percent in two years
news.title_en: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material have surged more than 8,400 percent in two years
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
of AI being used for the sexual exploitation of children have jumped more than 8,400 percent in two years. According to a report by Edinburgh's Childlight Institute, the number of reported AI-generated abuse images climbed from about 4,700 in 2023 to over 400,000 in 2025, The Guardian reports. The material includes AI-manipulated images (deepfakes) from so-called "nudify apps" that digitally strip people of their clothing. Abusers can use the faked images to blackmail children into handing over money or more photos.

The data comes from reports that tech companies filed with the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). The UK's Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) reviewed 6,310 criminal, photorealistic AI-generated abuse images in the first half of 2026 alone. That's 40 percent more than in all of 2025.

Childlight data director Debi Fry acknowledges that better detection systems partly explain the spike. She still calls for swift action from lawmakers and tech companies. Childlight CEO Paul Stanfield wants governments to classify the problem as a preventable public health emergency, dedicate funding to prevention, and coordinate efforts across healthcare, schools, child protection services, and the justice system.AdAd

news.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in its second mega-round within six months
news.title_en: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in its second mega-round within six months
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Alphabet's AI drug discovery company Isomorphic Labs has raised $5 billion, its second billion-dollar round in six months. Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital co-led the round, joined by new backer Andreessen Horowitz along with Alphabet and all existing investors.

The company had already raised $2.1 billion back in May 2026. The money will go toward advancing its in-house platform IsoDDE (Isomorphic Drug Design Engine) and pushing its drug pipeline toward clinical trials. IsoDDE goes beyond AlphaFold 3, according to the company founded in 2021, and aims to better predict drug binding and docking sites. Isomorphic Labs works with Novartis, Eli Lilly, and Johnson & Johnson but has no approved drug to show for it yet.

The company is led by Demis Hassabis, who stepped down from day-to-day leadership of Google Deepmind in August 2026 and now serves as Alphabet's Chief Scientist. Hassabis won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside John Jumper for their work on AlphaFold.Ad

Deepmind's original AlphaFold team was disbanded in July 2026. Many researchers moved to Isomorphic Labs or were reassigned to other projects. Nearly a quarter left Deepmind entirely. Deepmind still shipped AlphaGenome 2 in early November 2026, which predicts how DNA variants affect gene activity in specific cell types.Ad

ai_analysis.digest_en:
Alphabet's AI drug discovery company Isomorphic Labs has raised $5 billion, its second billion-dollar round in six months. Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital co-led the round, joined by new backer Andreessen Horowitz along with Alphabet and all existing investors.

The company had already raised $2.1 billion back in May 2026. The money will go toward advancing its in-house platform IsoDDE (Isomorphic Drug Design Engine) and pushing its drug pipeline toward clinical trials. IsoDDE goes beyond AlphaFol

核心事实：Isomorphic Labs 在六个月内第二轮大型融资中筹集了 50 亿美元

key_points_en: Key Development: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in its second mega-round within six months

news.article_content_zh:
Alphabet 旗下的人工智能药物发现公司 Isomorphic Labs 筹集了 50 亿美元，这是六个月内的第二轮 10 亿美元融资。 Greenoaks 和红杉资本共同领投此轮融资，新投资者 Andreessen Horowitz 以及 Alphabet 和所有现有投资者也跟投。

该公司早在 2026 年 5 月就已筹集了 21 亿美元。这笔资金将用于推进其内部平台 IsoDDE（同构药物设计引擎），并将其药物管道推向临床试验。该公司成立于 2021 年，表示 IsoDDE 超越了 AlphaFold 3，旨在更好地预测药物结合和对接位点。 Isomorphic Labs 与诺华 (Novartis)、礼来 (Eli Lilly) 和强生 (Johnson & Johnson) 合作，但尚未有批准的药物可供展示。

该公司由 Demis Hassabis 领导，他于 2026 年 8 月辞去 Google Deepmind 的日常领导职务，现在担任 Alphabet 的首席科学家。哈萨比斯 (Hassabis) 与约翰·詹珀 (John Jumper) 因其在 AlphaFold.Ad 上的工作荣获 2024 年诺贝尔化学奖

Deepmind 最初的 AlphaFold 团队于 2026 年 7 月解散。许多研究人员转移到 Isomorphic Labs 或被重新分配到其他项目。近四分之一的人完全离开了 Deepmind。 Deepmind 仍于 2026 年 11 月上旬推出了 AlphaGenome 2，它可以预测 DNA 变异如何影响特定细胞类型中的基因活性。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】美国证券交易委员会 (SEC)：Isomorphic Labs 在六个月内第二轮大型融资中筹集了 50 亿美元
【起因与机理】巨额融资意向凸显出头部模型公司在研发前沿架构与构建超级计算集群过程中巨大的资本消耗率，企业正力求在公开上市前锁定充沛流动性以构筑壁垒。
【关键数据与实测】Isomorphic Labs 在六个月内第二轮大型融资中筹集了 50 亿美元。
【各方立场与态度】美国证券交易委员会 (SEC)在全球产业与技术前沿一线。
